author: ojiudezue
title: v5.85.1 shipped: fix: a room sensor can be removed again (SENSCAP-ORPHAN-1)
summary: Operator hit sensor_capabilities_invalid on every submit in Garage Hallway and could not clear a noisy camera person sensor. Root cause is an ordering trap, not a validation bug: the capability dropdowns are built from the PRE-EDIT CONF lists, so removing a sensor still submits its caps_kind selection; derive_capability then returns None for the now-unwired entity, the no-op branch is missed, and the else-branch writes a declaration the very next validate rejects. Chose to PRUNE de-wired declarations rather than relax the validator, because the validator's rejection is correct and its own error text tells the operator to fix it by editing the CONF lists — which is exactly what they did. First version of the fix broke four existing tests (test_v4516_failsafe_freshness extracts that region verbatim and execs it standalone, so an outer-scope name raised NameError); caught only by a full-suite NAME diff against a baseline worktree — a count diff would have misread four broken existing tests as my four new tests failing.

refs.release_notes:
- Removing any sensor from any room was impossible whenever the per-entity capability dropdowns rendered: the stale caps_kind dropdown for the just-removed entity was folded into an orphan capability declaration, which the validator then rejected as sensor_capabilities_invalid — re-rendering the same stale dropdown and wedging the form permanently.
- Fix prunes declarations for de-wired entities on BOTH paths (JSON blob before first validate, dropdown during fold).
- 4 new tests drive the real async_step_sensors handler; mutation-drill verified (2 failed neutered / 25 passed restored).
- Full-suite name-diff vs clean baseline worktree: zero new failures (141/141), +4 passing.
